correctness.rationale: The restriction axiom is pointwise on N_0^n; every count vector has strictly positive probability for positive finite Poisson intensities, so the a.s. bound is pointwise. On the all-positive vector the nonempty stopping set must be a singleton {j}. Comparing configurations differing only at j shows j belongs to every output; a fixed positive value at j forces immediate singleton output. The zero fiber is again a stopping-set map on n-1 coordinates, so induction yields one uniquely determined partial permutation stopped at first positive count. Conversely each such prefix map satisfies restriction; one-atom-at-a-time exploration yields it pointwise. The cardinality is sum_{r=0}^n n!/(n-r)!; budget two admits the explicit parity-dependent second query.
risks: Strictly positive finite intensities, deterministic rules, and the finite discrete location budget are essential; no assertion about diffuse, zero-intensity or infinite-site cases.
